messages:
inc-bot: PAGING oncall - streaming p99 tail latency exceeded for /v1/stream (SLO 350ms -> observed 1.2s). Severity: sev2. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1825009876 :rotating_light:
ashok: ack, taking this. Oncall here — starting triage. Which AZs/peers showing the spike?
inc-bot: top affected AZs: us-east-2a -> us-east-2c cross-AZ traffic increased x3. TCP retransmits +25% on nat-gw-*-us-east-2c. TLS handshake RTTs also spiking.
ashok: running quick checks — kubectl logs show repeated websocket stalls, many connections hit 504 on upgrade. p95 still okay, p99 large tail.
ashok: starting tcpdump on nat-gw and one streaming pod (cmd):
```
# tcpdump -nni eth0 tcp and host 10.2.14.22
14:23:01.123456 IP 10.2.14.22.43012 > 10.3.7.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12400, ack 67890, win 64240, length 55
14:23:01.223789 IP 10.3.7.11.443 > 10.2.14.22.43012: Flags [.], ack 12400, win 65000, length 0
14:23:01.324000 IP 10.2.14.22 > 10.3.7.11: TCP retransmission
```
ashok: tcpdump shows repeated retransmits and occasional zero-length acks with dup ack pattern. Suspect packet loss or MTU path issues.
elaine: networking - we rolled a route advertisement change earlier this morning in us-east-2c for a test. I'll check combined routes and ENI metrics.
josh: cs - any customers calling in? Are we seeing major request errors (not just latency) in customer-facing dashboards?
ashok: most customers see degraded streaming experience (buffering, stalls). Error rate up for websocket upgrades ~2.7% (baseline 0.1%). No full dataplane outages.
networking-sre: quick network notes: BGP route flap avoided but route preference caused some pods in 2a to egress via 2c NAT (cross-AZ hairpin). That increases latency and ups retransmit risk. Also seeing PMTU blackhole indicators on some traces.
ashok: mitigation plan: 1) force same-AZ egress for streaming subnets (route table override) 2) scale per-AZ NAT gateways and move streaming egress to local NATs 3) enable tcp_mtu_fix on host kernel as temporary. I'll apply 1 and 2 now.
ashok: applying route override (example):
```
# aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-xyz (pin to local nat)
```
elaine: prepping AST to push NAT scale + healthcheck changes. ETA ~4m.
ashok: NAT scaled in us-east-2a/2b/2c, route overrides pushed, starting canary traffic shift for streaming route.
ashok: metrics update after route pin: p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms within 7m, retransmits -15%. p95 stable.
josh: noted. CS will message customers who reported streaming problems. quick blurb: "We observed transient streaming stalls impacting a subset of connections; mitigation in progress, we'll follow up with postmortem"
networking-sre: recommending follow-ups: run path MTU discovery tests across AZs, audit the morning route change, add a routing guard in deploy pipeline to prevent cross-AZ hairpin for streaming CIDRs.
ashok: enabling tcp_mtu_fix on streaming hosts as additional step. command: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`
ashok: after MTU probe enabled, p99 further improved to ~310ms and retransmits near baseline. Streaming stalls rate dropped ~90%.
ashok: marking incident as mitigated for customer impact. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours.
marta: taking handoff at T+45m to monitor. Summary for next oncall: root cause likely route preference change + cross-AZ egress causing path MTU and retransmit exposure; mitigations: route override + scale local NAT + enable MTU probing. Open action items: 1) roll back or re-review route advertisement change 2) add synthetic stream checks across AZs 3) document runbook steps + playbook commands.
marta: @elaine @networking-sre please own the route audit and prevention item.
elaine: on it — will find exact route change and PR author.
statuspage-bot: Status update posted: Investigating -> Mitigated (streaming degraded for some customers, mitigation applied, monitoring).
ashok: leaving detailed logs and tcpdump capture in /var/shared/incidents/1825009876.tar.gz for postmortem. cc @marta.
marta: ack, I'll coordinate postmortem and timeline. Leaving incident open for follow-up tasks; will close after audit and a follow-up postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
